images.title: Meet at an end, or intersect
images.purpose: Contrast two segments that meet at a shared endpoint with two segments that intersect at a point inside them.
images.composition: Two panels side by side with a thin grey divider; each holds one pair of segments; a short caption under each.
exact_structure: Left panel: two teal (#0072B2) segments FG and FH sharing the endpoint F, F at the left, opening to the right with 115.3 degrees between them, the angle marked by a reddish purple (#CC79A7) arc.
Left panel: the endpoint F is a dark dot and G and H are the other ends.
Right panel: a teal segment and an amber (#E69F00) segment crossing at point X, a dark dot, with X inside both segments and not at an end of either.
Right panel: the crossing is at about 60 degrees; no angle number is written there.
A short caption under each panel.
rejection: segments in the left panel not sharing the endpoint F
X placed at an end of a segment
images.takeaway: Segments can meet at an endpoint or intersect at a point inside them.
images.description: Left, two segments share the endpoint F with 115.3 degrees between them; right, two segments cross at the point X.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students match the words endpoint and intersect to the two pictures.

image_decisions.why: The two ways segments meet are the core of the concept.
